ops.title: tccd keys bare-CLI TCC grants by RESOLVED PATH (client_type=1) even with a dotted Dev-ID identifier — the identifier only lands in the row's csreq; durable grants need a stable real exec path, or an .app bundle (identifier-keyed)

ops.body: **Corrected 2026-07-08 (supersedes the v0.45.0 "identifier fix" belief).** macOS tccd keys a bare Mach-O CLI's TCC grants by the **literal resolved executable path** (`client_type=1`) — even when the binary is Developer ID signed with a dotted reverse-DNS identifier. Proven live: cc-pool 0.45.0–0.49.0 (five releases, all signed `com.yasyf.cc-pool`) each minted a fresh path-keyed `kTCCServiceSystemPolicyAppData` row for its Cellar path; the claimed v0.45.0 fix never changed keying (and was never really validated — cc-pool's *Network Volumes* rows stopped in the same window only because the fuse backend was retired). The dotted identifier is still load-bearing: it lands in the row's **csreq** (`identifier "com.yasyf.cc-pool" and anchor apple generic … subject.OU = TEAMID` — decode via `select hex(csreq)` → `xxd -r -p` → `csreq -r <file> -t`), which any future Dev-ID release satisfies. So the durable-grant recipe for a bare CLI is **stable identifier + stable real path** (symlinks don't count — tccd resolves them): cc-pool v0.49.1 has the daemon re-exec from `~/.cc-pool/bin/cc-pool` (fusekit `proc.ReexecStable`) before touching TCC-gated resources — one prompt at cutover, then upgrades silently revalidate. `.app` bundles at fixed paths get identifier-keyed rows instead (`client_type=0`, e.g. `com.yasyf.fusekit-holder`) and are Apple's prescribed shape for daemons needing durable grants. Adhoc/unsigned builds (`Identifier=a.out`) re-prompt per build regardless (cdhash csreq). Inspect: `sqlite3 -readonly ~/Library/Application\ Support/com.apple.TCC/TCC.db "SELECT service,client,client_type FROM access"`. Pre-granting TCC is impossible outside MDM PPPC, and SystemPolicyAppData has no MDM payload at all. See [[fp-backend-rollout]], [[cc-pool-fileprovider-signing-reality]], [[claude-pool-project]].
